parameters_passed_to_the_agent.search_scope: Calls for proposals of NWO (Dutch Research Council), the national research funder of the Netherlands, that are open, open for pre-proposals, continuous, upcoming or in preparation, and that fund thematic or programmed research in which companies, public bodies or other users can take part (as co-applicant, collaboration partner, co-funder or user-committee member), or that address the energy system, electricity grids, offshore wind and the North Sea, energy storage and conversion, materials for the energy transition, digital technology, AI, software and cybersecurity, infrastructure and spatial planning, climate adaptation, or societal transitions. This includes the NWO calls of European partnerships (for example CETPartnership, Driving Urban Transitions, Raw Materials Partnership), the Knowledge and Innovation Covenant (KIC) mission calls, the Dutch Research Agenda (NWA) calls and the Applied and Engineering Sciences (AES/TTW) programmes such as Perspectief, Open Technology Programme and KIEM. Out of scope: personal talent and career grants (Veni, Vidi, Vici, Rubicon, PhD and doctoral grants, scholarships), curiosity-driven open competitions without a theme (Open Competition, SSH Open Competition, Gravitation, Weave), small instruments that are not research funding (scientific meetings, open access books, science communication, computing time, top-ups for running NWO projects such as Impact Explorer or KIC top-up calls), entrepreneurship instruments for researchers (Take-off, Venture Challenge), research infrastructure rounds reserved for named roadmap consortia, and calls whose whole subject is health and medicine, food and agriculture, fisheries, cultural heritage and archaeology, humanities, polar or space science, fundamental chemistry, labour-market or workforce productivity, or semiconductor manufacturing equipment. A two-stage call whose compulsory pre-proposal deadline has passed is closed to new applicants: skip it, even when its full-proposal deadline is still ahead. A call whose mandatory first step for the main applicant has passed (a letter of intent, or registration for compulsory matchmaking or collaborative workshops) but whose pre-proposal or full-proposal deadline is still ahead stays in scope only because companies can still join an already registered consortium as user, cooperation partner or co-funder; record it and say so in the record. Calls with status 'In preparation' are out of scope until NWO publishes their call text (the status then changes to 'Open for applications', 'Open for pre-proposals' or 'Upcoming'): their page gives only a short description, an indicative closing date and budget, and no eligibility or participation rules, so their record could only be a thin Type 3 that later runs cannot update. A later run records them once the call text is out.
parameters_passed_to_the_agent.navigation_instructions: 1. The starting URL is the English call finder (www.nwo.nl/en/calls) filtered on six status values: In preparation (62162), Open for applications (1866), Open calls (62286), Continuous (1868), Open for pre-proposals (62164) and Upcoming (1869). 'In progress' (62165, 1870) means the call has closed and proposals are being assessed, and 'Closed' (1867) is out of scope. If the filter ids no longer match these labels, select the labels in the 'Status' filter yourself. 2. The listing is server-rendered: a plain page fetch (curl) returns the cards, so no browser is needed. Each page shows 12 cards; go through every page with &page=0, &page=1 and so on, using the page numbers in the pager at the bottom of page 0, and do not stop at the first page that repeats earlier calls. The site's default sort is by closing date and its order is not stable between page loads, so cards can repeat on one page and be missing from another; the starting URL therefore sorts by title (sort_bef_combine=nwo_entity_title_ASC), and the run should still collect the unique call links of all pages before screening (on 2026-11-17 the filtered list held 46 unique calls on pages 0 to 4). The facet counts in the Status filter overlap ('Open calls' contains the 'Continuous' calls), so do not use them to check completeness. The card status label is often missing in the listing, so read the status on the call page. 3. Screen each card's title and short description against the search scope. 4. Open each call page (www.nwo.nl/en/calls/<call>). The 'Characteristics' box at the side gives the status, the pre-proposal and full-application closing dates with time, the total budget and the research programme. The main text has the sections Purpose, Who can apply, Consortium building, What to apply for, When to apply, Assessment, and on the Prepare and Submit tabs the Call for proposals PDF and the application forms. All tabs are in the same HTML page, so one fetch gets everything, including the document links (href ending in .pdf, .docx or .xlsx). The 'Characteristics' box is the quickest reliable source for the status and the deadlines. 5. 'In preparation' pages carry a disclaimer: the call is not yet approved by the NWO Executive Board, the closing date and budget are indicative, and some sections are empty. Record such a call as forthcoming from the indicative closing date and the description; the final call text appears later on the same page and in the Staatscourant. 6. The Call for proposals PDF (linked from the call page, under www.nwo.nl/sites/nwo/files/media-files/) is the authoritative text for eligibility, consortium roles (main applicant, co-applicant, collaboration partner, co-funder), co-funding requirements, budget modules and deadlines; for some calls (for example Perspectief) NWO states that the Dutch version is authentic. Call PDFs often have generic file names (for example Call-for-Proposals_EN.pdf), so check pdfs/ for a file with the same name from another call before saving. For a European partnership call, NWO's page and NWO's national requirements set the Dutch rules; the partnership's call text and portal give the transnational rules. 7. Many NWO consortium calls (KIC, NWA, Perspectief) require registration for matchmaking or collaborative workshops before the proposal, or a compulsory pre-proposal or letter of intent; note such deadlines, because a missed mandatory step can close the call to new applicants. 8. Calls that NWO lists for an application round in a later year are separate FOs from earlier rounds of the same programme. 9. Participation routes seen in NWO calls: only researchers at Dutch research organisations may be main applicant; companies and public bodies take part as user, cooperation partner or co-funder (cash or in kind at fixed Dutch government hourly rates) and never receive the NWO grant, which usually makes a call Type 2 for TenneT. Perspectief also requires a co-lead on behalf of the users, and NWA calls allow 'societal organisations' as de-minimis-funded co-applicants (at most EUR 300,000 over three years), where it is unclear whether a company such as TenneT qualifies. 10. Record fields: organization_or_parent_framework is 'NWO (Dutch Research Council)' with the NWO Domain where the page names one; programme is the instrument line (for example 'Dutch Research Agenda (NWA)', 'Knowledge and Innovation Covenant (KIC)', 'Perspectief'); call_year is the year in the call title or round, otherwise the opening year stated in the call text.
parameters_passed_to_the_agent.link_scope: Call pages under www.nwo.nl/en/calls/ and their Dutch versions under www.nwo.nl/calls/, the call documents they link to under www.nwo.nl/sites/nwo/files/, NWO's own pages on funding rules (www.nwo.nl/en/laws-and-regulations-concerning-funding, partnership and co-funding rules), the Staatscourant publication on zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl, and for a European partnership call the partnership's own call page and call documents (for example cetpartnership.eu, dutpartnership.eu). Do not follow links to ISAAC (NWO's application system) or any login page, the NWO project database, news, events or vacancies, or external programme websites other than the partnership call documents.
parameters_passed_to_the_agent.completion_rules: The run is complete when every page of the filtered call finder has been screened and every call within the search scope has been opened. If the run reaches the cap of 5 new candidates first, stop there: later runs skip the calls already recorded and find the rest. A run that screens everything and finds no new call ends with no new FO.
